item.title: AI‑Generated Sci‑Fi Film *Gods Don’t Give Gifts* Adds Grimes
item.description:
AI‑Generated Sci‑Fi Film Gods Don’t Give Gifts Adds Grimes

AI‑generated sci‑fi anthology Gods Don’t Give Gifts is set to open in theatres on Dec 4, and it has added pop‑star Grimes, who will provide both her likeness and vocal performance.

🔍 Overview

  • Billed as “the first AI film to come to theatres.”
  • Produced by AI studio Fable.
  • Release date: December 4 (the film releases in December).
  • A trailer for the film has been released.

🎬 Cast & Creativity

  • Grimes will appear, lending both her likeness and vocal performance.
  • Grimes’s involvement is described as giving the project some legitimacy.
  • Grimes is also working on an AI‑themed album titled Psy Opera.

🎥 Production Details

  • Directed by Jack London, better known online as Gossip Goblin.
  • The work is an anthology of four interconnected stories set in a future where bodies are disposable and consciousness is commoditized.
  • Fable’s press release states: “casting the likeness of an actor with their spoken vocal performance will become more common with animated films using AI: audiences will see actors, athletes, musicians giving vocal performances with their likeness in films.”

📚 Themes

  • The setting depicts a world where bodies are disposable and consciousness is commoditized.
  • It explores the horrifying consequences of humanity’s attempt to transcend the flesh.
  • These themes align with Grimes’s past interest in transhumanism and artificial intelligence.

📈 Industry Context

  • The film is presented as a notable test case for the commercial potential of AI films.
  • While there has been hype about AI in Hollywood, no project has yet shown the technology as a vital storytelling tool.
  • Previous AI‑generated attempts, such as two versions of The Odyssey (including one made with Elon Musk’s Grok), “left plenty to be desired.”
Aspect Detail

item.title: Fountain 0 Releases AI Generated Film Odysseus: The Fall
item.description:
Fountain 0 Releases AI Generated Film Odysseus: The Fall

AI firm Fountain 0 has released a new film titled Odysseus: The Fall, which is described as “the first completely AI generated film produced at the level of a Hollywood blockbuster.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Production: Written and directed by company cofounder Ash Koosha, who created all the music and lent his likeness to the title character.
  • Motivation: Koosha stated he adapted the story because he “always felt passionately about Homer’s epic tale since [he] originally read it years ago.”
  • Studio History: The studio’s only previous work was an AI film called Dreams of Violets that was featured in Tribeca earlier this year.

🚀 Availability

  • Price: Available to rent for $9.99.
  • Platform: Viewable via a web browser.

🔍 Observations

Because current AI models are only capable of generating scenes lasting a few seconds, the film is described as a disjointed collection of moments stitched together. Reported technical and narrative issues include:

  • Visual Inconsistencies: The height of the cyclops changes between shots, oars bend and twist, a sword transforms into a dagger, and waves move in the opposite direction of the wind.
  • Animation Errors: Mouths do not match spoken words (sometimes moving without sound), and one boat in a fleet is seen moving sideways.
  • Audio Issues: AI-produced voice-overs can be incomprehensible, and the names of Zeus and Odysseus are pronounced incorrectly.
  • Character and Plot: Characters exhibit baffling acting with unexplained pauses and bursts of laughter. The plot structure is disjointed, with Penelope’s suitors not introduced until the movie is nearly over.
  • Visual Style: Hyperreal human characters are contrasted with monsters that look like “shabby stop-motion creatures from the 1930s.”
  • Anomalies: One scene features an alien carcass roasting over a spit.
